children: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena raised its 2026 pretax profit guidance and reported higher third-quarter profit, as it considers a 34.3 billion-euro ($38.49 billion) takeover offer by Intesa Sanpaolo.

The Italian lender said Friday that it now expects to report 2026 pretax profit above 3.7 billion euros, up from above 3.6 billion euros previously. It reported pretax profit of 2.075 billion euros in 2025.

The guidance doesn't include the potential impact of Italy's 2027 budget, which the bank said is still being assessed. The budget increases the national corporate tax rate for banks to 30.5% from 27.5%.

Monte dei Paschi said net profit for the third quarter was 542.9 million euros, up from 474.0 million euros a year ago. Analysts had forecast net profit of 468.4 million euros, according to consensus estimates compiled by Visible Alpha.

The bank said total revenue rose 8.7% to 2.00 billion euros. Net interest income increased to 1.11 billion euros from 1.02 billion euros, while net fee and commission income grew to 593.3 million euros from 573.5 million euros.
Net interest income was supported by higher lending volumes, Monte dei Paschi noted.
The company restated its 2025 nine-month figures to include its acquisition of Mediobanca for comparison, leaving net group profit unaffected.
Monte dei Paschi said its CET1 ratio was 16.4% at the end of September. It forecast a CET1 ratio of around 15.5% at the end of 2026.
Shareholders in Monte dei Paschi--which is widely considered to be the world's oldest bank still in operation--will soon decide whether to support Intesa's offer or remain independent.

The acceptance period for Intesa's bid will start in late November. Intesa has received authorization from the European Central Bank for the takeover, but is still awaiting approval from the Italian markets regulator, with a decision expected early next week.

Monte dei Paschi had been seeking to fend off Intesa's offer. However, its plans were upended last week when shareholders overwhelmingly rejected twin bids to buy Banca Generali and Banco BPM, proposed by Chief Executive Officer Luigi Lovaglio in an attempt to thwart Intesa's takeover.
Despite Lovaglio's previous statements of opposition, Monte dei Paschi hasn't formally endorsed or rejected Intesa's offer yet.
Monte dei Paschi said on Friday that it is still analyzing Intesa's offer, a review that it aims to finish by the end of this month.

Intesa is offering 1.25 euros in cash and 1.6 of its shares for each Monte dei Paschi share. This will increase to 1.644 of its shares after an interim dividend is paid. The bid values Monte dei Paschi at around 34.3 billion euros based on Thursday's closing prices.
